claims.text: Transition metal dichalcogenides such as MoS2 can provide enhanced catalytic activity for the hydrogen evolution reaction.
Transition metal dichalcogenides such as MoS2 can provide enhanced durability during the hydrogen evolution reaction.
Transition metal dichalcogenides such as MoS2 can provide enhanced catalytic activity for the hydrogen oxidation reaction.
Transition metal dichalcogenides such as MoS2 can provide enhanced durability during the hydrogen oxidation reaction.
Doping or defect engineering of pristine transition metal dichalcogenides produces catalytically relevant edge sites or defects.
Edge sites and defects increase active-site density.
Doping or defect engineering improves charge transfer in transition metal dichalcogenides.
Increased active-site density and improved charge transfer enhance catalytic activity.
Doping or defect engineering enhances durability relative to pristine transition metal dichalcogenides.
The proposed material can operate in acidic or alkaline electrolytes and at elevated temperatures.
Performance is limited by material stability under the electrolyte and operating conditions.
